baseline: Wave 1 evaluation: 16 synthetic cases (13 independent), one AI-drafted annotator, engine 2026.3.1, knowledge pack 1.0.0
note: Written before any detector was changed. Categories are the primary reason the engine did not report a labelled signal; alsoNeeds lists other things the same event needs. The labels were drafted by an AI assistant: a miss can also be a labelling issue.

F01.name: Intermittency phrases
F01.fix: A typed phrase family for "sometimes works, sometimes not" (sometimes/now and then/occasionally/off and on + works/fails/goes through/signs in), "comes and goes", and "not constant/consistent/every time", read only in a clause that also speaks of failing or signing in.
F01.risk: medium: "sometimes" is common outside failures; the clause must carry a failure or sign-in word.
F01.test: Positive: six wordings per alternative. Negative: "sometimes I forget my password", "not constant bandwidth"; negation: "this is not intermittent".

F02.name: Other sites are fine
F02.fix: A family for "colleagues/users/staff at <other> office/site have no trouble / are fine / unaffected" that does not need the literal words "other sites".
F02.risk: medium: any unaffected group is read as a site pattern; require a place word and a contrast with the affected group.
F02.test: Positive: four wordings. Negative: "everyone at our office is affected", "the other team is on holiday".

F03.name: Name-resolution error in words
F03.fix: Allow words between "name" and "could not be resolved" ("the name of the server could not be resolved"), "could not resolve the host", "DNS lookup failed", in a sentence about the client or sign-in.
F03.risk: medium: printers and other products report the same words; require the sign-in or Teams context in the same sentence.
F03.test: Positive: five wordings. Negative: the printer look-alike case (z3) must still report nothing.

F04.name: No records in the sign-in logs, in words
F04.fix: A family for "nothing/no failures/no rows/no entries/not a single record ... for those attempts/users", with the log check named in the same event (title included), including the passive "no failures are recorded".
F04.risk: medium: a request "please check whether there are no records" must not fire (modality handles requests).
F04.test: Positive: six wordings. Negative: "we expected no records", "if there are no records, escalate"; conflict with the present-side signal when both are stated.

F05.name: A name server does not answer
F05.fix: A family for one of several name servers or resolvers that does not answer, times out or stays silent while the others answer, with a count ("four of the five tries") or a contrast ("while the other one is fine").
F05.risk: medium: "does not answer" about a person; require resolver, name server or DNS words or an address pair.
F05.test: Positive: five wordings. Negative: "the customer did not answer my email", "both name servers answered".

F06.name: A network change is reported
F06.fix: Broaden the verb family (switched on, rolled out, put in place, introduced) and the object family (filtering policy, inspection profile, web filter), accept the network admin role as the context, and let the object be "that server" or "the cluster" when the event answers a question about changes.
F06.risk: high: "change" statements are common; keep the role gate and a policy/filter/profile noun.
F06.test: Positive: six wordings by a network admin. Negative: a change to a printer, a change that is planned ("we will switch on"), a denied change.

F07.name: A fix worked (reported in prose)
F07.fix: These two signals can only be read from structured data today. A text reading needs three things: recognising the customer-side remediation ("I removed it from the DHCP scope", "took proxy-04 out of the load balancer"), a generic success statement ("since the change every sign-in worked"), and linking them across events. Not attempted before the dev set can measure it.
F07.risk: high: a success statement without the link says nothing about which cause was right.
F07.test: Cross-event cases in the corpus; property test that the signal needs both the remediation and the success statement.

F08.name: Timeout reported in words
F08.fix: Read "the connection timed out", "timed out at login", "times out when they open Teams" as the client timeout when the sentence is about the client, users or sign-in.
F08.risk: medium: the printer look-alike also "timed out"; require the sign-in, Teams, users or client context in the same sentence.
F08.test: Positive: five wordings. Negative: printer and print-server look-alikes, "the report timed out".

F09.name: Clearing the cache or reinstalling did nothing
F09.fix: Let the outcome follow the action across a sentence boundary within the same event ("did a full reinstall. No difference, ...", "nothing changed"), and read "did both/it" as the step the engineer asked for in the event it answers.
F09.risk: medium: an outcome phrase without an action in the reply must resolve through the request it answers.
F09.test: Positive: reply after a request, with and without the action named. Negative: an outcome phrase answering a different request.

F10.name: Revoking sessions: request and outcome
F10.fix: Recognise the engineer asking for "sign out everywhere", "drop old sessions" as the revoke step, and read "same failures as before" in the reply as its outcome.
F10.risk: medium: sign-out requests are also routine hygiene; require the session wording.
F10.test: Positive: request and reply pairs. Negative: sign-out for another purpose.

F11.name: Proxy comparison reported by the engineer
F11.fix: The signal is read only from customer-side events; the engineer ran this test, so accept the engineer roles and the engineer e-mail and diagnostic types.
F11.risk: low: the same statement by the engineer is evidence of the same kind; gated by the proxy wording.
F11.test: Positive: engineer diagnostic result and engineer e-mail. Negative: an engineer request to test the proxies (modality).

F12.name: An access policy was changed
F12.fix: Broaden the subject (access rule or policy, security policy, compliance rule, session policy, sign-in frequency) and the recency (day names, "two weeks ago", "last week", "on Friday") beyond the literal "Conditional Access policy ... yesterday".
F12.risk: medium: "policy" is generic; keep the access/security/session noun and a change verb.
F12.test: Positive: six wordings. Negative: "we will change the policy", "no change was made", a password policy.

F13.name: Log findings described in prose
F13.fix: Read "failed attempts are in the sign-in logs", "stopped by Conditional Access", "interrupted multi-factor step", and "errors 70043 and 700082 ... token has expired" as the log findings, with or without the AADSTS prefix.
F13.risk: medium: a request to look for them must not fire (modality); code numbers need the log context.
F13.test: Positive: eight wordings. Negative: "check whether the logs show CA failures", an unrelated five-digit number.

F14.name: Excluding a user did nothing
F14.fix: Recognise the engineer asking to exclude or leave a user out of "that rule" and read "still blocked, same message" in the reply as the outcome.
F14.risk: medium: exclusion is a security-weakening step; the outcome must be tied to the request.
F14.test: Positive: request and reply pairs. Negative: an exclusion that worked.

F15.name: A denial reported as the fact
F15.fix: A modality layer: a denied, guessed, planned or conditional statement is not read as the fact, and a denial of one side of a declared signal pair is read as the other side ("nothing active" is "no active incident").
F15.risk: low to medium: cue reach is bounded and every cue has fires and look-alike examples; see docs/EVALUATION.md.
F15.test: The four known-defect tests become passing tests; adversarial negation tests for every cue.

F16.name: Only one user or device is affected
F16.fix: A family for "only me", "just my laptop/this device", and "my colleagues/teammates ... are fine", read together with a failure in the same message.
F16.risk: medium: "only me" without a failure is not a scope statement; require a failure or sign-in word in the event.
F16.test: Positive: five wordings. Negative: "only me in the meeting", "not just one user" (negated).

F17.name: The device has no primary refresh token
F17.fix: A family for "no primary refresh token", "PRT is missing", "does not have a PRT", read as a statement about the device.
F17.risk: low: specific vocabulary; the negation is the content.
F17.test: Positive: four wordings. Negative: "there is a primary refresh token".

F18.name: Chat style: typos and abbreviations
F18.fix: A bounded normalisation of the scanned text with a fixed list of common abbreviations and typos (ppl, pls, u, r, thru, somtimes, peple, agian, ...), with an offset map so every match and excerpt still points into the stored text. No fuzzy matching.
F18.risk: low: a fixed, reviewed list; each entry is whole-word and has a test.
F18.test: Offsets and excerpts verify against the stored text; every entry has a positive and a look-alike; property test: normalisation never moves a match outside the original text.

F19.name: Access policy unchanged, said with a negative quantifier
F19.fix: A family for "nothing was changed in our access policies", "no changes to the conditional access", "we have not touched the policy", with the broadened subject of F12.
F19.risk: low to medium: the negation is the content; the subject must be an access or security policy.
F19.test: Positive: five wordings. Negative: "something was changed", "the printer policy is unchanged".

F20.name: A message written in another language
F20.fix: Not fixed. The engine reads English only. The case is kept in the set as a known limit; a language-specific pack would be a separate piece of work.
F20.test: The case stays labelled; the metrics report it as out of scope.
